data.title: Revenue Beat: Inari Amertron Berhad Exceeded Revenue Forecasts By 17% And Analysts Are Updating Their Estimates
data.description:

It was a decent earnings report, with revenues and statutory earnings per share (EPS) both performing well. Revenues were 17% higher than the analysts had forecast, at RM369m, while EPS of RM0.016 beat analyst models by 12%. The analysts typically update their forecasts at each earnings report, and we can judge from their estimates whether their view of the company has changed or if there are any new concerns to be aware of. Readers will be glad to know we've aggregated the latest statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their mind on Inari Amertron Berhad after the latest results.

After the latest results, the 19 analysts covering Inari Amertron Berhad are now predicting revenues of RM1.45b in 2027. If met, this would reflect a solid 18% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Per-share earnings are expected to jump 98% to RM0.07. In the lead-up to this report, the analysts had been modelling revenues of RM1.46b and earnings per share (EPS) of RM0.073 in 2027. So it looks like there's been a small decline in overall sentiment after the recent results - there's been no major change to revenue estimates, but the analysts did make a minor downgrade to their earnings per share forecasts.

It might be a surprise to learn that the consensus price target was broadly unchanged at RM2.76, with the analysts clearly implying that the forecast decline in earnings is not expected to have much of an impact on valuation. There's another way to think about price targets though, and that's to look at the range of price targets put forward by analysts, because a wide range of estimates could suggest a diverse view on possible outcomes for the business. The most optimistic Inari Amertron Berhad analyst has a price target of RM3.50 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at RM1.85. There are definitely some different views on the stock, but the range of estimates is not wide enough as to imply that the situation is unforecastable, in our view.

Of course, another way to look at these forecasts is to place them into context against the industry itself. One thing stands out from these estimates, which is that Inari Amertron Berhad is forecast to grow faster in the future than it has in the past, with revenues expected to display 24% annualised growth until the end of 2027. If achieved, this would be a much better result than the 4.7% annual decline over the past five years. By contrast, our data suggests that other companies (with analyst coverage) in the industry are forecast to see their revenue grow 17% per year. Not only are Inari Amertron Berhad's revenues expected to improve, it seems that the analysts are also expecting it to grow faster than the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The biggest concern is that the analysts reduced their earnings per share estimates, suggesting business headwinds could lay ahead for Inari Amertron Berhad. Happily, there were no major changes to revenue forecasts, with the business still expected to grow faster than the wider industry. The consensus price target held steady at RM2.76, with the latest estimates not enough to have an impact on their price targets.

data.title: KCTech's (KRX:281820) Earnings Are Of Questionable Quality
data.description:
Investors were disappointed with KCTech Co., Ltd.'s (KRX:281820) earnings, despite the strong profit numbers. We did some digging and found some worrying underlying problems.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Examining Cashflow Against KCTech's Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

KCTech has an accrual ratio of 0.25 for the year to September 2026. Therefore, we know that it's free cashflow was significantly lower than its statutory profit, which is hardly a good thing. To wit, it produced free cash flow of ₩39b during the period, falling well short of its reported profit of ₩100.1b. KCTech's free cash flow actually declined over the last year, but it may bounce back next year, since free cash flow is often more volatile than accounting profits. One positive for KCTech shareholders is that it's accrual ratio was significantly better last year, providing reason to believe that it may return to stronger cash conversion in the future. Shareholders should look for improved cashflow relative to profit in the current year, if that is indeed the case.

Our Take On KCTech's Profit Performance

KCTech's accrual ratio for the last twelve months signifies cash conversion is less than ideal, which is a negative when it comes to our view of its earnings. Because of this, we think that it may be that KCTech's statutory profits are better than its underlying earnings power. But at least holders can take some solace from the 65% EPS growth in the last year. Zooming In On Kbi Metal's Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Kbi Metal recorded an accrual ratio of 0.32. Therefore, we know that it's free cashflow was significantly lower than its statutory profit, raising questions about how useful that profit figure really is. In the last twelve months it actually had negative free cash flow, with an outflow of ₩54b despite its profit of ₩28.8b, mentioned above. We saw that FCF was ₩1.4b a year ago though, so Kbi Metal has at least been able to generate positive FCF in the past. Unfortunately for shareholders, the company has also been issuing new shares, diluting their share of future earnings. One positive for Kbi Metal shareholders is that it's accrual ratio was significantly better last year, providing reason to believe that it may return to stronger cash conversion in the future. And so, you can see quite clearly that dilution is having a rather significant impact on shareholders.

If Kbi Metal's EPS can grow over time then that drastically improves the chances of the share price moving in the same direction. However, if its profit increases while its earnings per share stay flat (or even fall) then shareholders might not see much benefit. For that reason, you could say that EPS is more important that net income in the long run, assuming the goal is to assess whether a company's share price might grow.

Examining Cashflow Against Sungdo Engineering & Construction's Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Sungdo Engineering & Construction recorded an accrual ratio of -0.22. That implies it has very good cash conversion, and that its earnings in the last year actually significantly understate its free cash flow. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of ₩69b, well over the ₩12.7b it reported in profit. Sungdo Engineering & Construction's free cash flow improved over the last year, which is generally good to see. Having said that, there is more to consider. data.title: Could Broader Mortgage Score Access Just Shift FICO's Investment Narrative?
data.description:
• FICO reported that Xactus will now offer the monthly FICO Preferred Program to all mortgage industry clients, bundling Classic FICO Score and FICO Score 10T at a wholesale price of US$10 per bureau, per borrower, with extended availability through the XedaLink and SharperLending platforms.
  • The expanded distribution and fixed bundle pricing give Fair Isaac wider reach into mortgage workflows, which could influence how reliably lenders access its high margin Scores business during a period of competitive and regulatory pressure.
  • We will now assess how this broader FICO Preferred Program distribution through Xactus could reshape Fair Isaac's investment narrative for investors.

Compare how Fair Isaac’s mortgage focused scores story stacks up against a curated group of resilient financials by scanning the 31 resilient stocks with low risk scores in one sweep.

Fair Isaac Investment Narrative Recap

To own Fair Isaac, you need to believe the Scores franchise can keep pulling in high quality earnings even as mortgage pricing power comes under pressure. According to andre_santos, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote the Narrative, the big swing factor is how much profit Fair Isaac keeps from its mortgage related Scores. The Xactus deal looks helpful for keeping FICO scores embedded in lender workflows, but it does not remove competitive or regulatory risk.

The near term catalyst is execution on the Direct Licensing and Preferred Program rollout that andre_santos sees as central to the story, while managing a higher debt load and recent restructuring. The biggest risk remains share or pricing loss to VantageScore in US mortgages, which the fixed US$10 bundle does not fully address. This announcement feels incremental rather than transformational for that debate.

The most relevant recent move is the appointment of Julie May as President of B2B Scores, given how much Fair Isaac still relies on the Scores segment. Her background across product development, fraud, cybersecurity and go to market work lines up with what the Preferred Program and reseller expansion require, especially as lenders weigh using multiple scores in parallel.

If Fair Isaac executes well under May, the Xactus rollout could support the catalysts that andre_santos highlights, such as keeping margins supported by high scoring profitability and making better use of reseller channels. Investors still need to weigh that against the stated risks, like higher leverage, volatile share performance and the possibility that lenders shift more volume toward cheaper alternatives despite these partnerships.

On andre_santos' numbers, Fair Isaac reaches a fair value of US$632.72 a share if revenue compounds at 4.7% a year and the business settles at a 26.0% profit margin. Together, these factors support strong cash generation in the model without relying on the higher growth and profitability seen in earlier scenarios.

Uncover why Fair Isaac's fair value indicates a 9% potential downside to its current price, which leaves little room for error.

Exploring Other Perspectives

Some analysts frame the key catalyst very differently. Where the baseline stresses mortgage pricing risk, the most optimistic forecasts lean on FICO Platform momentum and assume revenue rising to about US$3.1b with earnings near US$1.2b by 2029. Those projections were set before this Xactus news, so you may want to revisit them and compare multiple viewpoints.
